**Iridium's handler structure repair is verified against the current source.** [The independent AST audit](implementation/status-20260906-iridium-handler-repair/ast-original-review.json) found that ICC had extended the existing `KeyboardHandler` implementation inside `keyboard/mod.rs`. The registered two-file repair moved that type and implementation into a 415-line named file, preserving its public path and behavior; the module is now 118 lines. [Independent rereview closed ICC-AST-01](implementation/status-20260906-iridium-handler-repair/ast-repair-review.json): all 40 Rust files in the 43-path source set were scanned, with zero skips or parser errors. Nineteen inherited inventory matches and the unrelated 2,877-line editor core remain explicitly qualified, so there is no aggregate AST-clean claim. [Fresh local proof](implementation/status-20260906-iridium-handler-repair/iridium-handler-local-proof.json) records 403 focused keyboard tests plus complete core, syntax and TUI selections, full workspace tests, strict workspace Clippy, wasm check/Clippy and formatting against exactly `e785bb9ecf5bf4174c7d3ea5b5871b4a4d90bb844605fde43bdd9acd8d5fd6a2`. Full workspace tests passed 3,209 cases with zero failures; [the 20 baseline ignores and actual GPU target counts](implementation/status-20260906-iridium-handler-repair/iridium-handler-workspace-test-census.json) are recorded. The first retry could not find a Metal adapter; that failed result is preserved alongside the successful run in the GPU-capable context. [The R3 syntax-cache ownership closure](implementation/status-20260906-iridium-handler-repair/iridium-r3-independent-closure-addendum.json) is now persisted; its initial review remains unchanged. Earlier 42-path tests and benchmark measurements remain historical. The approximately 70 ms Rust stress cost remains unresolved. Explicit operator stop/pause pauses the queue; failure or cancellation does not silently advance it.
Coordinate queued and channel inputs through one admission owner; expose partial fan-out outcomes and avoid duplicate retries.
Preserve queue records across host detach; define restart recovery so uncertain submissions are never silently replayed.
checkpoints.done_when: Queue three messages, observe three sequential turns, then pause and edit the remainder without losing or duplicating input.

checkpoints.title: Independent session host and attach/detach
scope: Move live provider, tools, MCPs, queue, cwd and root cancellation ownership out of the TUI into a Norn host.
First checkpoint: one independently running session and read-only observer; second: interactive attach/detach to that same session.
Attach receives semantic Ready state then ordered updates; history and large bodies load on demand.
Detach, cancel-turn and stop-session are separate; no Aion dependency, PTY replay or server-rendered terminal frames.
Start sessions with hosting support; do not claim arbitrary old foreground processes can be adopted.
Show actual session cwd without claiming to change the invoking parent shell; define version compatibility and control authority.
checkpoints.done_when: Start background work, attach, detach during a tool, and reattach to the same session and running work with no replayed effects.

checkpoints.title: Additive feature activations
scope: Use /plan, /goal and /coordinate as independently composable feature activations, not exclusive operating modes; remove /implement.
Persist and display active features; define their target scope, inheritance and changes during active work.
The user request determines whether planning means design, writing a plan, executing it, or a combination; activation alone does not authorize new effects.
Additional user instructions can tailor the planning process and deliverables, with their scope and provenance retained.
Feature activation does not broaden permissions; explicit operator stop overrides every activation.
checkpoints.done_when: Activate planning and coordination together, tailor planning with additional instructions, and verify the runtime and UI agree without requiring an implement mode.

checkpoints.title: Linked goals, plans and tasks
scope: Keep goals (desired outcomes), plans (approaches/designs) and tasks (units of work) as distinct records with stable identities and explicit typed links.
A goal can have plans and tasks attached; a plan can address goals and organize tasks; a task can contribute to goals and implement a part of a plan.

Allow useful standalone records and multiple links rather than forcing every record into a rigid goal-plan-task hierarchy. Planning will often involve a goal; existing goals should be linked rather than duplicated.
Use the existing task hierarchy, dependencies and assignments where applicable; linking and dependency ordering are distinct relationships.
Show related records and progress in the pane and expose the same authoritative state through structured tools.
Version plan changes and preserve link integrity. Link creation or task completion must not silently complete a goal, grant authority, or trigger execution.
Preserve linked-record scope and provenance through delegation; define missing/deleted record and dependency-cycle behaviour in the implementation brief.
checkpoints.done_when: Open a goal, inspect its attached plan and tasks, navigate the links in both directions, and revise or execute the plan under the user request without maintaining duplicate checklists.

checkpoints.title: Goal activation and completion protocol
scope: Connect objective, optional budgets and explicit completion conditions to linked plans and tasks; support standalone goals and goals used during planning.
Distinguish implementation complete, validation complete, merged and installed; attach concrete evidence.
Enforce pause, blocked and completion semantics; budget limits and queue behaviour remain explicit.
checkpoints.done_when: Run a bounded goal, pause it mid-work, resume it deliberately, and finish only when its stated conditions are met.

checkpoints.title: Coordination activation
scope: Use the same directory, @ addressing, tasks and queues for delegation, ownership, handoff and acknowledgements.
Make delegated scope, dependencies and current ownership visible; prevent duplicate assignment and unacknowledged handoff claims.
Scope coordination permissions and feature inheritance explicitly; stopped coordination must not launch fresh work.
checkpoints.done_when: Delegate independent tasks to two agents, inspect each conversation, and see acknowledged results update the shared plan.

checkpoints.title: Text-to-speech
scope: Define a typed output subscriber and service adapter for an existing user-selected speech service.
First ship final-message read-aloud with play/stop/replay/voice settings; streaming speech is a later checkpoint.
Keep playback off the agent stop-hook/control path; start adapters only when enabled/used.
Bind speech to selected session/output identity and keep local audio ownership with the attached client.
checkpoints.done_when: Read an assistant response aloud, stop it immediately, replay it and change voice without blocking agent execution.

checkpoints.title: Speech-to-text
scope: Define capture/transcription adapters for an existing user-selected service.
Start with push-to-talk into Iridium; provisional recognition remains separate until committed to the draft.
Bind recognition to recipient and draft revision; preserve edits and do not misdeliver after switching agents.
Make direct voice submission a later explicit preference, with visible recording/cancellation/errors.
checkpoints.done_when: Dictate, correct the resulting draft and send using the configured send key; switching agents during recognition cannot retarget it silently.

checkpoints.title: Tool inspection and Markdown composer polish
scope: First independent delivery: syntax highlighting in the Changes/diff pane using the existing syntax highlighter, with path-derived language, syntax-coloured code and distinct added/removed markers/backgrounds. Preserve displayed text, wrapping and selection/copy. Cache highlighted evidence in the existing background job; never parse syntax during paint or scrolling.

Diff pane follows the latest eligible recorded change by default. Direct inspection (scrolling, selecting/copying text, choosing an older change, or later editing) pins the view and prevents automatic replacement. A visible Latest/resume-follow control returns to the newest change and resumes following; no guessed idle timeout steals the view. Following the diff must not retarget the composer, change the conversation scroll position or admit provider input. Publish only completed matching-revision evidence so stale background jobs cannot replace newer content.
Give tool groups clearer styling and selected/expanded backgrounds.
Present arguments as readable fields with a raw input toggle; make shell commands prominent.
Add Markdown editing conveniences and lazy highlighting only inside language-tagged code fences.
Keep startup, input, scroll and resize measurements; the known cached-row lookup optimization remains named work, not a completed fix.

Context usage: show estimated next input tokens divided by the active configured context-window limit as a percentage in the existing status area, with used/limit available. Do not use cumulative billed tokens or assume the model maximum when a smaller limit is configured. Distinguish estimates and unavailable/stale measurements; update on new authoritative estimates and compaction. Show any output reservation or compaction threshold separately rather than silently changing the denominator.

Tool presentation: vary semantic colours and grouping, add subtle selected/expanded backgrounds and distinct running/success/failure/blocked states, while retaining tool name plus tool_use_description. Keep labels/symbols so colour is not the only cue. Preserve readable contrast, terminal capability handling, selection/copy, compact height and incremental repaint behaviour.
checkpoints.done_when: Watch successive edits automatically appear with syntax highlighting; inspect an older diff without it being replaced, then resume Latest. Wrapping/copy and the composer remain intact. Subsequent deliveries improve tool forms and Markdown writing.

checkpoints.title: Editable workspace and session controls
scope: Build on read-only Changes with Iridium file editing, explicit change baselines and guarded saves when agents also edit files.
Persist auxiliary pane selection and provide Work/Session controls for tasks, agents, model settings, prompts, skills and tool access.
Keep the composer full width, optional conversation/workspace side-by-side, and no global header consuming vertical space.
checkpoints.done_when: Review and edit a changed file beside the conversation; concurrent changes cannot silently overwrite each other.

checkpoints.title: Request-time output contracts
scope: Attach validated output schemas to individual interactive or driven requests with provider-enforced support where available.
Expose structured output as an alternate request/result view while preserving the conversation.
Specify inheritance through queued messages, children and host attachment; do not treat structured output as only a global runtime switch.
checkpoints.done_when: Send a schema-bound request, inspect its structured result, then send an ordinary request in the same session.

checkpoints.title: Modular extension interfaces
scope: Keep an opinionated Norn product with typed, replaceable service/tool/view interfaces.
Use Liminal for stack interoperability; speech adapters provide a bounded first extension case.
Reconcile with Manifold before adding a general module host; Meridian is not the intended future path.
Validate generation changes and in-flight calls during replacement; load services lazily and expose failures.
checkpoints.done_when: Replace one adapter without restarting or corrupting an unrelated running session; broader hot-loaded tools/views require their own proof.

preserved_separate_work: Public releases, supported platform matrix, one-line installer/updater and rollback.
Venue source-binding and exact-commit battery/review work; do not claim missing receipts passed.
Unfinished Claude SDK integration and archived prototype branches need independent reconciliation.
Branch/worktree and inactive-build cleanup after merged content and rollback are verified.
Voluntary game/play integrations remain product use cases, not hidden evaluation work.
